exercises.name: Mountain Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Feet, calves, quads, glutes, deep core, postural muscles
instructions: Stand with your big toes close and heels slightly apart, or feet hip-width if that feels steadier.
Lift and spread your toes, set them down, and balance your weight evenly across both feet.
Firm your thighs without locking the knees and stack hips over ankles and shoulders over hips.
Let your arms hang with palms forward, level your chin, and breathe slowly for the full hold.
exercises.formCue: Ears over shoulders, shoulders over hips, hips over ankles.
exercises.commonMistakes: Locking the knees back and letting the ribs flare forward so the lower back arches.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stand with feet hip-width apart, or with your back lightly against a wall to feel the stacked line.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the stacked, balanced stance every other standing pose is built from.

exercises.name: Standing Forward Fold
exercises.musclesWorked: Hamstrings, calves, glutes, lower back
instructions: Stand tall with hands on your hips and feet hip-width apart.
Hinge forward from the hips, keeping the front of your torso long as you lower.
Rest your hands on the floor, on blocks, or on your shins and let your head hang heavy.
Keep a soft bend in the knees and shift a little weight toward the balls of your feet.
Come up by bending the knees and rising with a long back.
exercises.formCue: Fold from the hips, not the waist.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding hard through the lower back to reach the floor, or locking the knees and pulling on the hamstrings.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees generously and rest your hands on blocks or a chair seat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lengthens the whole back of the body and is the linking position in most flows.

exercises.name: Half Lift
exercises.musclesWorked: Spinal erectors, hamstrings, glutes
instructions: Start in a standing forward fold with feet hip-width apart.
Place your fingertips on the floor, on blocks, or on your shins.
Breathe in and lift your chest until your back is flat and roughly level with the floor.
Reach the crown of your head forward, keep the back of your neck long, then fold again on the breath out.
exercises.formCue: Flat back, long neck, chest forward.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the upper back, or cranking the head up and pinching the neck.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees slightly and put your hands on your shins or thighs so the back can flatten.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains a clean hip hinge with a long spine, which carries into every forward bend and lift.

exercises.name: Chaturanga (Plank to Low Plank)
exercises.musclesWorked: Triceps, chest, front shoulders, core
instructions: Set a strong plank with shoulders over wrists and legs firm.
Shift forward a little so your shoulders move just ahead of your wrists.
Bend your elbows straight back along your ribs and lower in one piece.
Stop when your upper arms are about level with the floor and elbows sit over wrists.
Hold for a breath, then press back up or move on to your next pose.
exercises.formCue: Elbows hug the ribs, body moves as one board.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the shoulders below elbow height, or letting the hips sag or pike.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower your knees to the floor first and keep the same straight line from knees to head.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the pressing strength and shoulder control that keep flowing sequences safe.

exercises.name: Upward-Facing Dog
exercises.musclesWorked: Spinal erectors, glutes, triceps, chest, hip flexors
instructions: Lie face down with legs hip-width apart and hands on the floor beside your lower ribs.
Press the tops of your feet into the floor so your thighs switch on.
Breathe in, straighten your arms, and lift your chest and thighs off the floor.
Stack wrists under shoulders, draw your shoulders back, and keep your neck in line with your upper back.
Hold for a few breaths, then lower down or lift the hips to Downward Dog.
exercises.formCue: Thighs off the floor, chest pulls forward and up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Hanging in the shoulders with them up by the ears, or sagging into the lower back with relaxed legs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the thighs and hips on the floor and bend the elbows for Cobra Pose.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the chest and front of the hips while strengthening the arms and back.

exercises.name: Warrior One
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, hip flexors, calves, shoulders
instructions: Step one foot forward between your hands and bend that knee over the ankle.
Turn your back heel down so the back foot angles about 45 degrees.
Press the back thigh straight and firm the outer edge of the back foot into the floor.
Rise up, turn your chest toward the front, and reach both arms overhead.
Hold for five to ten breaths, then switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Back leg strong, front knee tracks over the ankle.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the front knee cave inward, or dumping into the lower back as the arms go up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the stance, take the feet wider side to side, and keep hands on hips.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds leg strength and opens the hip of the back leg in one hold.

exercises.name: Triangle Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Hamstrings, inner thighs, obliques, glutes, shoulders
instructions: Stand with feet wide, front foot turned out and back foot turned slightly in.
Reach your arms out level with your shoulders and keep both legs straight but not locked.
Reach forward over the front leg, then tip from the hip and lower your front hand to your shin, a block, or the floor.
Stack the top arm over the bottom arm and open your chest to the side.
Hold for five breaths, press through the feet to rise, and switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Long on both sides of the waist.
exercises.commonMistakes: Collapsing the bottom side of the torso to reach the floor, or locking the front knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rest your bottom hand on a block or high on the shin and keep a small bend in the front knee.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It stretches the hamstrings and inner thighs while teaching the legs to hold a steady base.

exercises.name: Extended Side Angle
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, inner thighs, obliques, shoulders
instructions: Start in a wide stance with the front foot turned out and arms reaching out to the sides.
Bend the front knee toward 90 degrees, keeping it over the ankle.
Lean over the front leg and place your forearm on the thigh or your hand outside the front foot.
Sweep the top arm over your ear so your body makes one line from back heel to fingertips.
Hold for 30 to 60 seconds, then rise and change sides.
exercises.formCue: One long line from back heel to top fingertips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the front knee drift inward, or sinking all the weight onto the bottom arm.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rest the forearm lightly on the front thigh, or put the bottom hand on a block.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the legs while lengthening the whole side of the body.

exercises.name: Half Moon Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, outer hips, hamstrings, ankles, obliques
instructions: From Triangle Pose, bend the front knee and look down at the floor.
Place your bottom hand a little ahead of the front foot, under the shoulder, on the floor or a block.
Shift your weight onto the front leg and lift the back leg until it is level with your hip.
Straighten the standing leg without locking it and turn your chest open to the side.
Reach the top arm up, hold for a few breaths, then step back down with control.
exercises.formCue: Flex the lifted foot and push it into an imaginary wall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Locking the standing knee, or letting the top hip roll forward so the chest faces the floor.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a tall block under the bottom hand and practise with your back near a wall.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains single-leg balance and outer-hip strength at the same time.

exercises.name: Tree Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, outer hips, calves, feet, deep core
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose and shift your weight onto one foot.
Place the sole of the other foot on the inner calf or inner thigh of the standing leg, never on the knee.
Press foot and leg into each other and keep your hips level and facing forward.
Bring your hands together at your chest, or reach them overhead once you are steady.
Fix your eyes on one point, hold, then change sides.
exercises.formCue: Foot into leg, leg into foot.
exercises.commonMistakes: Resting the foot against the side of the knee, or hiking the hip of the lifted leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the toes of the lifted foot on the floor with the heel on the ankle, or stand next to a wall.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds ankle and hip stability and the focus needed for every balance.

exercises.name: Eagle Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, outer hips, upper back, shoulders
instructions: Stand tall, bend both knees, and shift your weight onto one leg.
Cross the other thigh over the standing thigh and hook the foot behind the calf if you can.
Reach your arms forward, cross one elbow over the other, and wrap the forearms so the palms meet.
Lift your elbows to shoulder height, sit a little lower, and keep your chest upright.
Hold for about five breaths, unwind, and repeat on the other side.
exercises.formCue: Sit low, lift the elbows, squeeze everything to the midline.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing up tall out of the squat, or tipping the chest forward to stay balanced.
exercises.beginnerModification: Cross the legs and rest the top toes on the floor like a kickstand, and hold opposite shoulders with the arms.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It challenges balance while stretching the upper back and outer hips.

exercises.name: Bridge Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors, chest, hip flexors
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width apart, close to your hips.
Rest your arms by your sides with palms down.
Breathe in, press through your feet, and lift your hips.
Keep your thighs parallel, and if it is comfortable, clasp your hands under you and roll the shoulders in.
Hold for several breaths, then lower your spine slowly to the floor.
exercises.formCue: Press the heels down and keep the knees pointing straight ahead.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the knees splay out, or flattening and pressing the back of the neck into the floor.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift only part way, or rest your hips on a block for a supported version.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the chest and hips while strengthening the whole back of the body.

exercises.name: Boat Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Abdominals, hip flexors, spinal erectors, quads
instructions: Sit with knees bent, feet on the floor, and hands behind your thighs.
Lean back a little with a long spine until you balance just behind your sitting bones.
Lift your feet so your shins are level with the floor.
Reach your arms forward beside your legs, and straighten the legs only if your back stays long.
Hold for 10 to 20 seconds, building toward a minute, then lower with control.
exercises.formCue: Chest lifted, lower back long.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back and sinking the chest once the legs go up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the knees bent and hold the backs of your thighs, or keep the toes on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds deep abdominal and hip flexor strength with an upright spine.

exercises.name: Low Lunge
exercises.musclesWorked: Hip flexors, quads, glutes, groin
instructions: From Downward Dog or hands and knees, step one foot forward between your hands.
Lower the back knee to the floor and rest the top of the back foot down.
Keep the front knee over the ankle and slide the back knee away until you feel the front of that hip stretch.
Lift your chest and reach your arms overhead, or keep hands on your hips.
Hold for up to a minute, then switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Tailbone down, front of the back hip opens.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to lift the chest, or letting the front knee slide far past the toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pad the back knee with a folded blanket and keep your hands on blocks or on the front thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the hip flexors and quads that tighten up from sitting.

exercises.name: Lizard Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Hip flexors, inner thighs, hamstrings, glutes
instructions: From a low lunge, walk the front foot toward the outer edge of the mat.
Bring both hands to the floor inside the front foot.
Stay on your hands, or lower your forearms to the floor or to blocks.
Keep the back knee down for an easier hold, or lift it and press the heel back for more load.
Keep your chest reaching forward, hold for five slow breaths, then change sides.
exercises.formCue: Chest forward, hips level.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the upper back to get the elbows down, or letting the front knee collapse inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the back knee on a pad and stay up on your hands or on blocks.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It reaches the deep hip and inner-thigh range that lunges and squats depend on.

exercises.name: Half Splits
exercises.musclesWorked: Hamstrings, calves, glutes
instructions: Start in a low lunge with the back knee on the floor and hands framing the front foot.
Shift your hips back until they sit over the back knee.
Straighten the front leg and flex the foot so the toes point up.
Keep your hips square and walk your hands forward with a long spine.
Hold for five to ten breaths, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Lead with the chest, not the forehead.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the spine to chase the shin, or letting the hips drift back past the knee.
exercises.beginnerModification: Put blocks under your hands and keep a small bend in the front knee.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates one hamstring at a time without loading the lower back.

exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold
exercises.musclesWorked: Hamstrings, calves, spinal erectors
instructions: Sit with both legs straight in front of you and your feet flexed.
Breathe in and sit tall through the crown of your head.
Breathe out and hinge forward from the hips, keeping the spine long.
Walk your hands forward as far as is comfortable, holding your shins, feet, or a strap.
Lengthen a little on each breath in, ease forward on each breath out, and hold for one to three minutes.
exercises.formCue: Reach the chest toward the toes, not the head toward the knees.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling hard with the arms and rounding the back to get lower.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit on a folded blanket, bend the knees, and loop a strap around the feet.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives the hamstrings and back a long, calm stretch that suits the end of a session.

exercises.name: Bound Angle Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Inner thighs, groin, outer hips, spinal erectors
instructions: Sit tall, bend your knees, and bring the soles of your feet together.
Draw your heels toward your pelvis only as far as is comfortable.
Hold your ankles or feet and let your knees fall out to the sides.
Lift through your chest and keep your pelvis upright rather than slumped.
Stay for one to five minutes, then lift the knees with your hands and stretch the legs out.
exercises.formCue: Sit tall and let the thighs release on their own.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pushing the knees down with the hands or elbows, or slumping through the lower back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit on a folded blanket and rest blocks or cushions under each thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It opens the inner thighs and hips while training an upright seated posture.

exercises.name: Happy Baby
exercises.musclesWorked: Inner thighs, glutes, hamstrings, lower back
instructions: Lie on your back and draw both knees toward your chest.
Hold the outer edges of your feet, or your shins or the backs of your thighs.
Open your knees a little wider than your torso and bring them toward your armpits.
Stack each ankle over its knee so the shins point straight up.
Press your feet gently up into your hands as you draw down, and hold for several slow breaths.
exercises.formCue: Tailbone heavy, shoulders soft.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the head and shoulders, or curling the tailbone far off the floor to reach the feet.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold behind the thighs, or do one leg at a time with the other foot on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It releases the inner hips and lower back with no load on the spine.

exercises.name: Legs Up the Wall
exercises.musclesWorked: Hamstrings, calves, lower back (passive)
instructions: Sit sideways next to a wall with one hip close to it.
Lower onto your side, roll onto your back, and swing your legs up the wall.
Shuffle your hips toward the wall until your legs rest comfortably; they do not have to touch it.
Rest your arms by your sides with palms up and let your legs relax.
Breathe slowly for five to ten minutes, then bend your knees, roll to one side, and pause before sitting up.
exercises.formCue: Let the wall hold your legs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Forcing the hips tight to the wall so the hamstrings pull and the lower back lifts.
exercises.beginnerModification: Move your hips further from the wall, bend the knees, or rest your calves on a chair seat instead.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is a simple, fully supported position for winding down after training.

exercises.name: Corpse Pose
exercises.musclesWorked: Whole body (relaxation)
instructions: Lie on your back with legs straight and feet hip-width apart or wider, letting the feet fall out.
Rest your arms a little away from your sides with the palms up.
Lengthen the back of your neck and let your body feel heavy on the floor.
Soften your jaw and face, close your eyes, and let your breath slow down on its own.
Stay for at least five minutes, then roll to one side before you sit up.
exercises.formCue: Nothing to hold, nothing to fix.
exercises.commonMistakes: Skipping it, or lying there while planning the rest of the day.
exercises.beginnerModification: Put a rolled blanket under your knees and a thin cushion under your head.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives the body time to settle so the work of the session can sink in.

exercises.name: Garland Pose (Deep Squat Hold)
exercises.musclesWorked: Ankles, calves, inner thighs, glutes, lower back
instructions: Stand with feet a little wider than your hips and toes turned out slightly.
Bend your knees and lower your hips all the way down between your heels.
Bring your palms together and press your elbows gently against your inner knees.
Lift your chest and lengthen your spine while the knees track over the toes.
Hold for 30 to 60 seconds, then press through the feet to stand.
exercises.formCue: Heels heavy, chest tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the heels float with no support, or collapsing the chest and rounding the back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Put a folded blanket under your heels, sit on a low block, or hold a door frame for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It restores the ankle and hip range that a comfortable full squat needs.

exercises.name: Sun Salutation A
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, chest, triceps, core, hamstrings, hip flexors
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose, breathe in and sweep your arms overhead, then breathe out and fold forward.
Breathe in to a Half Lift, then breathe out, step back to plank, and lower through Chaturanga.
Breathe in to Upward-Facing Dog, then breathe out and lift your hips to Downward Dog.
Hold Downward Dog for three to five breaths, then step or walk your feet to your hands.
Breathe in to a Half Lift, breathe out to fold, then rise with arms overhead and return to Mountain Pose.
exercises.formCue: One breath, one movement.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rushing ahead of the breath, and letting the hips sag in the plank and lowering phase.
exercises.beginnerModification: Drop the knees for the lowering phase and swap Upward-Facing Dog for Cobra Pose.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It warms the whole body and links breath to movement in under a minute per round.

exercises.name: Hip Controlled Articular Rotation
exercises.musclesWorked: Hip flexors, glutes, deep hip rotators, obliques
instructions: Stand tall beside a wall or chair, hold it lightly, and brace your trunk so the pelvis stays still.
Lift one knee straight up in front of you as high as you can without leaning back.
Open the knee out to the side, then turn the thigh inward so the foot swings out and back behind you.
Lower the knee under your hip, then reverse the whole circle back to the start.
Move slowly enough that each circle takes several seconds, and stay inside a pain-free range.
exercises.formCue: Biggest circle you can make with nothing else moving.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the leg with momentum, or tilting and twisting the pelvis to fake a bigger circle.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it on hands and knees, where the floor steadies the trunk, and make a smaller circle.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It takes the hip through its full active range so you keep the motion you already own.

exercises.name: Shoulder Controlled Articular Rotation
exercises.musclesWorked: Rotator cuff, deltoids, upper back, serratus
instructions: Stand tall with ribs down, one arm straight by your side, and the other hand in a light fist.
Raise the working arm forward and up, thumb leading, until it is beside your ear.
At the top, turn the arm inward so the palm faces out and continue reaching back and down behind you.
Finish with the back of the hand near your hip, then reverse the path to the start.
Move slowly, keep the torso still, and stay inside a pain-free range.
exercises.formCue: Slow circle, quiet ribs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the back or leaning the torso to get the arm further, and rushing through the stiff part.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stand side-on to a wall an arm's length away and trace a smaller circle beside it.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the shoulder through its full active range before pressing, pulling, or hanging.

exercises.name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Drill
exercises.musclesWorked: Calves, soleus, Achilles tendon, ankle joint
instructions: Face a wall in a short split stance or half kneel with your front toes a few centimetres from it.
Keep the front foot pointing straight ahead and the heel flat on the floor.
Drive the front knee forward over the middle toes until it touches the wall or the heel wants to lift.
Ease back and repeat for slow reps, moving the foot further from the wall only if the heel stays down.
Switch sides and compare the two ankles.
exercises.formCue: Heel glued down, knee over the middle toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the heel peel up, or letting the arch collapse and the knee dive inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the toes almost touching the wall and hold the wall for balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Better ankle bend lets the knees travel forward so squats and lunges sit deeper and feel steadier.

exercises.name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
exercises.musclesWorked: Thoracic spine, chest, lats
instructions: Sit on the floor with knees bent and place a foam roller across your mid-back, below the shoulder blades.
Support your head with your hands and keep your elbows pointing forward and up.
Keep your hips on the floor and your ribs down, then lean back gently over the roller.
Pause for a breath, curl back up, and repeat a few times.
Shift the roller a little higher and repeat, staying on the upper and middle back only.
exercises.formCue: Hips down, ribs down, bend from the upper back.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the hips or flaring the ribs so the lower back arches instead of the upper back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a rolled towel instead of a roller and take a smaller range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It restores upper-back extension, which overhead reaching and good posture both need.
